lines.text: Manasseh becomes king at twelve, reigns fifty-five years, and rebuilds the high places his father Hezekiah tore down.
Manasseh builds altars in both courtyards of the LORD's house and sacrifices his sons in the Valley of Hinnom.
The LORD speaks to Manasseh and his people, they do not listen, and Assyria's commanders take him to Babylon.
Manasseh humbles himself and prays, and the LORD brings him back to Jerusalem, where he removes the idol and restores the altar.
Amon reigns twelve years, increases his guilt, and is killed by his servants, and the people make Josiah king.
